clues.text: This city stands along a river in the west of a long thin land in south Europe. Its old town spreads over seven hills by the water.
clues.narrowing: Rules out the east and north; puts the player on a river town of seven hills in the south west.

source.quote: Rome is located in the central-western portion of the Italian Peninsula, within Lazio (Latium), along the shores of the Tiber Valley.

clues.text: Summers here are hot and dry, with long bright days and little rain. Winters turn mild and wet, the flip side of those dry months.
clues.narrowing: Rules out wet summers and harsh winters; keeps the hot dry summer, mild wet winter pattern.

source.quote: with hot, dry summers and mild, humid winters

clues.text: Long ago this city ruled a vast empire as the seat of its rulers. In 1871 it became the capital of a newly united land, and it still is.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to an old empire's seat made capital of a newly united land in 1871.

source.quote: In 1871, Rome became the capital of the Kingdom of Italy, which, in 1946, became the Italian Republic.

clues.text: Gladiators once fought wild beasts in a huge stone ring here, the largest old arena still standing. It went up nearly 2,000 years ago and still draws crowds.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one huge old stone arena for gladiator fights still stands here.

source.quote: it was used for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles including animal hunts

clues.text: The chiefs of Italy rule the land from this city. A whole tiny land, the Pope's own, sits inside its bounds, a land in a city.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: Italy is governed here, and a whole tiny country sits inside the city.

source.quote: Vatican City—the smallest country in the world and headquarters of the worldwide Catholic Church under the governance of the Holy See—is an independent country within Rome's municipal boundaries

reveal.blurb: Old tales say a she-wolf raised the twin boys who founded this city in 753 BC, and it grew to rule a vast empire. Its huge stone arena, old ruins, and seven hills still draw crowds from all over the world. Rome is the capital of Italy.
